title: Matched online opponent-seat MGDA update smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: At the identity-complete iteration224 checkpoint, online minimum-norm aggregation of supported opponent-seat PPO and Standard10 source-KL gradients will produce strict common descent at matched ordinary actor-gradient norm on every update without breaking critic, replay, trust-region, assignment, or accounting contracts.
material_change: Branch the same immutable iteration224 checkpoint into matched ordinary-control and online-MGDA treatment continuations. Both preserve optimizer/replay/pool/league state, use identical fixed deals and restored assignment RNG, and run two updates; only treatment replaces policy-head actor gradients with norm-matched minimum-norm common descent.
baseline: Online ordinary-update audit at iteration221-224: all 8 probes harmed at least one objective; all 4 identity-complete probes harmed 4-5 of 11 objectives, while source-KL alignment was positive in 8/8.

notes: This is a two-update matched mechanism smoke. It cannot reject the long-horizon method or establish external strength. Admission requires strict positive intervention alignment, norm matching, unchanged control semantics, and clean continuation gates before any fresh breadth evaluation.

Both matched arms passed all nine source/staging gates from identical checkpoint SHA 5f6fdd6; both copied the same 224-row metric and assignment evidence and use fixed-deal start 21,100,000, beyond first-unused 20,102,255.

Both arms naturally stopped at iteration226. Because collection stops on a global decision boundary, scheduling produced 10,136 versus 10,166 new physical hands; the source checkpoint, fixed per-worker deal streams, first-iteration assignment state, optimizer/replay state and all configuration other than MGDA were matched. No result relies on reward comparison between the slightly unequal rollout suffixes.

All eight treatment optimizer minibatches had strict positive common-descent alignment across all eleven supported objectives. The minimum worst alignment was +0.12078; every intervention actor L2 matched the corresponding ordinary actor L2 within 9.22e-8 relative ratio error. Ordinary diagnostics remained conflicted in both arms.

result.summary: Two exact-state matched continuations completed about 10.1k new environment hands each. Control retained ordinary conflicted updates, while treatment executed eight norm-matched online MGDA steps with strict common descent for every supported opponent-seat and Standard10-KL objective. Both continuation audits and all 325 tests passed.
result.conclusion: The online conflict-aware optimizer is technically viable on the real replay-bearing integrated path: it changes only policy-head actor gradients, preserves critic and trainer state contracts, solves every observed simplex geometry, and removes local objective harm without increasing actor-gradient norm. This is mechanism evidence only; fresh frozen breadth must test translation and catastrophic drift before any geometric training scale.
result.next_step: Evaluate the frozen treatment versus matched ordinary control on untouched common-deck, both-seat Standard10/CFR4/legacy-iter16/legacy-mixed65k anchors and audit Standard10 capability drift. Use this as a catastrophe and direction gate, not as a small-sample method rejection; if stable/nonnegative enough, continue MGDA geometrically with multiple lineages.
